problems.title: Multiply mixed-number differences
problems.question: Evaluate (15-4⅛)(3¹⁴⁄₁₅-2⅗).
problems.idea: Convert each difference to a fraction.

problems.title: Cubic units in a large reservoir
problems.question: A rectangular reservoir measures 1.2 km by 0.8 km by 2.5 km. How many litres does it hold?

problems.title: Two divisibility rules at once
problems.question: 123AB is divisible by 36. How many distinct values can A+B have?
problems.idea: Divisibility by 36 means divisibility by both 4 and 9.
formulas: Digit sum divisible by 9; last two digits divisible by 4.
steps: The multiples of 36 from 12300 to 12399 are 12312,12348,12384.
There are two distinct sums: 3 and 12.

problems.title: Angle between the outer bisectors
problems.question: A straight angle is split in order in ratio 4:6:8. Find the angle between the first and last angle bisectors.
problems.idea: Add half the outer angles and the whole middle angle.
formulas: Straight angle=180°; angle bisector halves its angle.

problems.title: Recover total walking time
problems.question: Tourists walk 3/8 of a route, then 3/5 of the remainder. The final part takes 3 h 20 min. Their speed is constant. Find total walking time.
problems.idea: Time fractions equal distance fractions at constant speed.
steps: The last part is one quarter of the route.
Its 200 minutes therefore represent one quarter of total time.

problems.title: Units digits of two large powers
problems.question: Find the last digit of 199²⁰¹⁶-2016¹⁹⁹.
formulas: 9 to an even power ends in 1; any positive power of 6 ends in 6.
steps: The first power ends in 1 and the second in 6.
Their difference is congruent to 1-6=-5≡5 modulo 10.

problems.title: Triangles on two parallel lines
problems.question: Four points lie on one line and five on a parallel line. How many triangles use these points?
problems.idea: Choose two vertices on one line and one on the other.
steps: Two from the first and one from the second give C(4,2)·5=30.
These cases are disjoint and exhaust all noncollinear triples: total 70.

problems.title: Reverse a fractional comparison
problems.question: a is 2/3 of b. What percentage of a is b?

problems.title: Intersect and subtract finite sets
problems.question: A contains two-digit multiples of 9; B contains integers congruent to 3 modulo 4; C contains numbers below 100 ending in 3. Find |(A∩B)\C|.
formulas: Set difference removes elements in the second set.
steps: The two-digit multiples of 9 congruent to 3 modulo 4 are 27,63,99.
Only 63 ends in 3, so remove it.

problems.title: Percentage changes multiply for volume
problems.question: A box length and width rise 20%, while its height falls 25%. Find its volume change.
steps: The new volume is 108% of the original, an 8% increase.

problems.title: Read the walking sector
problems.question: The travel-to-school pie chart marks the metro sector 100° and bus sector 130°. What fraction walk?

problems.title: Difference of supplementary angles
problems.question: Two adjacent supplementary angles satisfy (2/7)A=0.4B. Find larger minus smaller.
problems.idea: Use their ratio and their sum.

problems.title: Midpoints along an ordered line
problems.question: A,B,C,D occur in that order with AC=8,BD=12,AD=17. Find the distance between the midpoints of BC and AD.
steps: The BC midpoint is 6.5, and the AD midpoint is 8.5.

problems.title: A straight-angle split around two crossing lines
problems.question: The vertical angles MOP,RON sum to 60°. Ray OS divides PON in ratio POS:SON=3:2. Find MOS as drawn.
problems.idea: Find the vertical angles before dividing the supplement.
formulas: Vertical angles equal; adjacent angles sum to 180°.

problems.title: Pairs of internal rays
problems.question: Ten distinct rays lie inside a 90° angle. How many angles have two of those ten rays as sides?
problems.idea: An angle is selected by an unordered pair of rays.
steps: Choose any two of the ten rays.
problems.note: This counts the ten interior rays specified in the question. If the two original boundary rays are also included, twelve rays instead give 66 angles.

problems.title: Supplementary angles in a 140% ratio
problems.question: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines satisfy A=140% of B. Find the larger angle.

problems.title: Use the two omitted angles
problems.question: Six of the eight angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines sum to 500°. Find the smallest angle.
problems.idea: Subtract from the total of all eight.
formulas: All eight angles sum to 720°; each is θ or 180°-θ.
steps: The two omitted angles sum to 720°-500°=220°.
They cannot be a supplementary pair, whose sum would be 180°. Thus they are equal, each 110°.

problems.title: Substitute remainders
problems.question: a≡2 and b≡3 modulo 7. Find the remainder of 4a-3b.

problems.title: A fraction between two decimals
problems.question: Which of 4/7,5/8,2/3,3/5,7/9,8/9 lies between 0.7 and 0.8?
problems.idea: Compare by cross multiplication or decimal values.
steps: 7/9>7/10 because its positive denominator is smaller. Also 7/9<4/5 because 35<36.
The first four fractions are below 0.7, and 8/9 is above 0.8.

problems.title: Angle between two transversals
problems.question: In the shown parallel-line diagram, the transversals give marked angles 30° and 125°. Find x.
formulas: Supplementary angles sum to 180°; corresponding angles are equal.
steps: The acute angle at the lower parallel is 180°-125°=55°.
The other transversal makes 30° with a parallel.

problems.title: Divisor count from prime exponents
problems.question: How many positive divisors does 81·125 have?
formulas: If N=pᵃqᵇ, its divisor count is (a+1)(b+1).
steps: A divisor chooses a 3-exponent from 0 to 4 and a 5-exponent from 0 to 3.

problems.title: Gcd times lcm gives the product
problems.question: Two positive integers have gcd·lcm=111 and differ by 34. Find their sum.
problems.idea: List factor pairs of their product.
steps: Only 37-3=34, so the numbers are 3 and 37.

problems.title: Complete the frequency table
problems.question: Scores 5,6,7,8,9,10 have frequencies 2,5,4,x,4,2 for 24 pupils. Find the missing frequency x.
formulas: Total frequency=24; median averages the two middle observations; mode is the most frequent value.

problems.title: Median of the completed table
problems.question: Scores 5,6,7,8,9,10 have frequencies 2,5,4,x,4,2 for 24 pupils. Find the median.
formulas: Total frequency=24; median averages the two middle observations; mode is the most frequent value.
steps: The completed frequencies are 2,5,4,7,4,2. The first eleven scores are at most 7.
Positions 12 and 13 both have score 8, so their average is 8.

problems.title: Mode of the completed table
problems.question: Scores 5,6,7,8,9,10 have frequencies 2,5,4,x,4,2 for 24 pupils. Find the mode.
formulas: Total frequency=24; median averages the two middle observations; mode is the most frequent value.
steps: Every other frequency is at most 5, so 8 is the unique most frequent score.
